key_findings.bandwidth_is_destiny: Single-stream decode is memory-bandwidth-bound. Tokens/sec scales with GB/s. V100 (900 GB/s) out-decodes every laptop-class Apple chip; only M3 Ultra (800 GB/s) competes.
key_findings.prefill_falloff_by_architecture: Linear attention (Mamba2, Gated DeltaNet) loses 7–11% from 512→32K. Full-attention MoE loses 18–20%. Dense loses 27%. GLM-4.7-Flash catastrophically loses 64%.
key_findings.build_value_winner: PRO 6000 leads bang-for-buck on 120B: 27.1 tok/s per $1,000, 0.58 tok/s per watt under load.
key_findings.multi_gpu_scaling: 4× B70 (TP=4, FP16 vLLM) scales 7–8× from 1→8 concurrent users. Q4 llama.cpp single-card 54.7 tg vs FP16 vLLM 4-card 16.3 tg—same hardware, different operating point.
key_findings.kv_quant_impact: Dense 40B tg falls 22→17 t/s (q4_0 KV). Dense 27B falls 33→24 t/s. MoE largely sidesteps via smaller KV cache.
key_findings.m5_vs_m3: M5 gains are in prefill (Neural Accelerators), not decode. M3 Ultra still Apple's decode king. M5 Max 614 GB/s trails M3 Ultra 800 GB/s.
